beats.say: More than twice as many cyclones as the Arabian Sea: the Bay of Bengal, from nineteen eighty-two to twenty twenty-four.
beats.caption: 1982–2024: Bay 120 · Arabian Sea 51 (IMD)

beats.say: This week's Cyclone Murasu is the latest. Why so many, and why so deadly?
beats.caption: Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu · Nov 2026

beats.say: One: warmth. The Arabian Sea is cooler, and India's weather office says that holds storms back.
beats.caption: 1 · Cooler Arabian Sea holds storms back (IMD)

beats.say: Two: a lid. After the monsoon, river water caps the north Bay, so storms stir up warm water.
beats.caption: 2 · Fresh-water lid (north Bay, after the monsoon)

beats.say: Three: the shape. At its head, the Bay narrows like a funnel, over shallow water.
beats.caption: 3 · At its head: a funnel over shallow water

beats.say: Storms push the sea in, and it piles up. That surge is the biggest killer.
beats.caption: The surge: the biggest killer (IMD)

beats.say: Warm water breeds them. The funnel makes them deadly.
beats.caption: Warm water breeds them. The funnel makes them deadly.
